title: Azure App Service

header.html: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (20-25%)

Provision an App Service plan; configure scaling for an App Service plan; create an App Service; configure certificates and TLS for an App Service; map an existing custom DNS name to an App Service; configure backup for an App Service; configure networking settings for an App Service; configure deployment slots for an App Service
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1App Service and the plan

Azure App Service is a managed platform (PaaS) for web apps, APIs and mobile back ends in .NET, Java, Node.js, Python, PHP and containers. Azure manages the OS, patching and load balancing.

The App Service plan is the compute the apps run on: it sets the region, operating system, size and features. Several apps can share one plan (they share its CPU and memory).

Tier Highlights
Free / Shared Dev and test, shared compute, no custom TLS, no scale-out
Basic Dedicated compute, custom domains and TLS, manual scale (up to 3)
Standard Autoscale, deployment slots, backups
Premium (v3) More slots and instances, faster hardware, zone redundancy
Isolated Dedicated environment in your VNet (App Service Environment)
Exam tip

. Deployment slots, autoscale and scheduled backups need Standard or higher.

2Scaling

Scale type Meaning
Scale up (vertical) Change to a bigger plan or tier (more CPU, memory, features)
Scale out (horizontal) Add instances of the app
Manual You set the instance count
Autoscale Rules (CPU, memory, HTTP queue) or a schedule change the count within min and max limits (Standard and above)

3Certificates, TLS and custom domains

Task How
Custom domain Needs Basic or higher; verify ownership with a TXT record (asuid) and add a CNAME (subdomain) or A (root) record
Certificates App Service Managed Certificate (free, auto-renews), certificate from Key Vault, or upload your own
TLS binding Bind the certificate to the custom domain (SNI SSL)
HTTPS Only Redirects HTTP to HTTPS
Minimum TLS version Set (for example 1.2) to reject older protocols

4Backup

Fact Detail
Tier Standard or higher
What App files, configuration and connected databases
Where A storage account container
Schedule Automatic backups are on by default in newer tiers; custom backups let you set the schedule and retention [Verify live]
Restore To the same app, a new app, or a slot

5Networking

Feature Direction Purpose
VNet integration Outbound Let the app reach resources in a VNet (databases, VMs)
Private endpoint Inbound Give the app a private IP so clients reach it privately
Access restrictions Inbound Allow or deny by IP, subnet or service tag
Hybrid connections Outbound Reach an on-premises TCP endpoint without opening inbound ports

6Deployment slots

A deployment slot is a live app with its own host name (for example myapp-staging) in the same plan.

Feature Fact
Swap Exchange the staging slot with production; the slot is warmed up first, so no downtime, and you can swap back
Slot settings Mark app settings or connection strings as slot settings so they stay with the slot during a swap
Traffic routing Send a percentage of production traffic to a slot for testing in production
Tier Standard or higher
Exam tip

. "Deploy a new version and switch with no downtime and an easy rollback" = deployment slot swap.

Exam tip

. Slot swaps, autoscale and backups need Standard or higher; custom domains need Basic or higher.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team wants to deploy a new version of a web app and switch to it with no downtime and an easy rollback. What should be used?

  • ADeleting the app and redeploying
  • BA deployment slot with a swap
  • CA resource lock
  • DA new subscription
Show the answer

Answer: B. Slot swaps warm up the new version and can be swapped back.

S2An app must add instances automatically when CPU is high. What is the minimum tier that supports autoscale?

  • AStandard
  • BFree
  • CShared
  • DBasic
Show the answer

Answer: A. Autoscale requires Standard or higher.

S3Which DNS record helps verify ownership of a custom domain for App Service?

  • AA TXT record
  • BAn MX record
  • CAn SOA record
  • DA PTR record
Show the answer

Answer: A. A TXT record with the asuid value verifies ownership.

S4A web app must connect to a database in a virtual network. Which feature fits?

  • AA private endpoint for inbound traffic
  • BA deployment slot
  • CVNet integration
  • DA backup
Show the answer

Answer: C. VNet integration provides outbound access to VNet resources.

S5Clients should reach an App Service only through a private IP address. What should be configured?

  • AVNet integration
  • BA deployment slot
  • CAutoscale
  • DA private endpoint
Show the answer

Answer: D. A private endpoint makes inbound access private.

S6An administrator wants an app setting to stay with the staging slot during a swap. What should be done?

  • ACopy it to production
  • BMark it as a slot setting
  • CRemove it
  • DAdd a tag
Show the answer

Answer: B. Slot settings are sticky to the slot.

7.2 Recall questions

R1What does an App Service plan define?

Show the answer

The region, operating system, size and features of the compute.

R2Which tiers support deployment slots?

Show the answer

Standard and higher.

R3What is the difference between scale up and scale out?

Show the answer

Scale up uses a bigger plan; scale out adds instances.

R4What does HTTPS Only do?

Show the answer

Redirects HTTP requests to HTTPS.

R5Is VNet integration inbound or outbound?

Show the answer

Outbound.

R6What is the free option for a certificate?

Show the answer

An App Service Managed Certificate.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Plan region, OS, size; apps share it; Standard+ for slots, autoscale, backup
Scaling scale up (bigger) vs scale out (more); autoscale rules or schedule
TLS and DNS Basic+ for custom domains; TXT verification; managed certificate; HTTPS Only
Networking VNet integration (out), private endpoint (in), access restrictions
Slots swap, slot settings, traffic routing, no downtime
